verifiedClaims: Initial trusted root inside the candidate repository is rejected before candidate content verification.
A self-consistent attacker root without the previous threshold is rejected before the release statement is read.
Root rollback, same-version equivocation, skipped rotation, expired final root, and partial old threshold are rejected.
A valid N to N+1 rotation requires both the old root threshold and the new root self-threshold.
A version-3 external monotonic checkpoint binds the root digest, release sequence, canonical signed-statement digest, and every accepted intermediate root.
Serialized checkpoint replacement prevents concurrent verifier runs from regressing an already accepted state.
A forked intermediate root cannot disappear inside a later apparently matching root chain.
The threshold-signed release statement binds tag, commit, tree, archive, freshness index, manifest, registry, and install inventory.
Archive substitution and tag-tree mismatch are rejected.
Git and OpenSSH are absolute, external, owner-controlled, executable, and digest-pinned.
The public metadata builder opens public keys and detached signatures only and refuses output overwrite.
Release manifest, install inventory, release index, and registry inputs are parsed with strict producer-format grammars and semantically joined before acceptance.
The deterministic release archive is required to reproduce the exact committed Git tree, including bytes, modes, member set, and normalized metadata.
Extra archive members, missing members, special files, duplicate paths, digest substitutions, stale release indices, and release-index equivocation are rejected.
Successful external verification remains ineligible to claim readyToInstall until downstream content and freshness gates pass.

releaseChainRegression.command: python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_fleet_parity tests.test_freshness tests.test_release_artifacts tests.test_trust_root

limitations: The suite uses ephemeral fixture keys. No production private key was created, accessed, or committed.
Production G1 acceptance remains pending a witnessed 2-of-3 offline ceremony, a protected checkpoint path, and two independently administered root-digest publication channels.
This is a narrow TUF-style root update implementation using OpenSSH sshsig, not a claim of full TUF client conformance.
The externally pinned Python runtime, clean loader environment, operating system, and protected custody paths remain part of the trusted computing base.
